# DotMail

> Gmail dot trick generator: create every dot variation of a Gmail username. Free, private, runs entirely in your browser.

DotMail relies on Gmail's built-in behavior of ignoring dots (.) in the username of an email address. That means j.ohn@gmail.com, jo.hn@gmail.com, and john@gmail.com all land in the same inbox. This tool generates every dot combination of one Gmail username. It's useful for filtering Gmail per service, tracing who leaked your email address, and organizing your inbox.

Fully client-side: no server, no database, no login. Your input and results never leave the browser.

## Key Facts

- Variations for an n-character username: 2^(n-1). Example: "john" (4 chars) yields 8 variations.
- Input limits: 2-18 characters (excluding dots), only a-z and 0-9.
- All variations route to the same Gmail inbox by Google's servers.

## FAQ

- What is the Gmail dot trick? A built-in Gmail feature that ignores dots in the username; every variation lands in the same inbox.
- Is it legal? Yes, official Gmail behavior, not an exploit.
- Is data stored? No, all computation is in the browser, no server.
- Does it work for multiple signups? Often not. More services normalize dots. The real value is filtering and leak detection.
